study.title: Automated and explainable coronary angiogram interpretation for selection of coronary artery bypass grafting candidates using artificial intelligence
study.venue: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery

imaging.modality_detail: Invasive coronary angiogram video clips (DICOM, 512 x 512 x L frames)
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries: left main, proximal/distal LAD, left circumflex, RCA

public_dataset_used.detail: MICCAI Segmentation and MICCAI Stenosis datasets (international competition benchmark) used in development data

annotation.annotator_expertise: Reference standard from cardiologist angiogram reports; training annotations by physicians with unclear formalized training

task.task_description: Seven-algorithm pipeline (left/right classification, non-coronary object detection, best-frame selection, anatomy segmentation, stenosis segmentation, stenosis registration, rule-based decision) detecting >50% stenosis in major coronary vessels and classifying patients as meeting AHA/ACC 2021 anatomic criteria for CABG.
task.clinical_application: Identification of CABG candidates from coronary angiograms to support guideline-directed revascularization and quality control

temporal_evidence.quote: followed by selection of the frame with maximum average contrast

method.pretraining: YOLOv8 and nnUNET fine-tuned for angiogram-specific tasks
method.explainability_method: Human-interpretable pixel-level segmentation overlays highlighting stenosis and anatomic segments

metrics.metric: Mean analysis time per video clip

G1.quote: This early technology was developed with a small, imperfect training set.

G2.quote: The cohort and comparison groups were highly selected with strict exclusion criteria not fully reflecting the depth and breadth of clinical practice.

G3.quote: A video-based training set from a broader clinical cohort would result in a more accurate reflection of realworld inputs.

G4.quote: The data source comprised 2-dimensional angiograms that can overlook eccentric lesions and valuable physiologic data.

G5.quote: A robust angiography model may require considerable ground truth annotations by experts, which is limited by financial and time constraints.

G6.quote: future testing of this technology should involve prospective study

G7.quote: Our models explain why stenosis is localized to specific arteries by highlighting relevant pixels and are thus human interpretable.

G9.quote: The training dataset also lacked situations such as prior stents, pacemakers, or totally occluded arteries.

G10.quote: Future work may require robust multi-institutional data-sharing agreements.

G12.quote: the potential for automated report generation, which is a capability of our pipeline but not thoroughly explored in this investigation

other_limitations: Reference standard from clinical reports may over- or underestimate disease
Model limited to major vessels; diagonal, ostial and posterolateral branches excluded
Training annotations by physicians with unclear formalized training
Errors from incorrect maximum contrast frame selection
Clinical context for surgery not always clear
future_work: Annotate a larger number of angiograms
Include greater lesion variation such as chronic total occlusion and variable anatomy
Incorporate Medina bifurcation classification, tortuosity, calcification and bypass anatomy
Embed in electronic medical record to flag patients for heart team discussion
